recon.notes: Squarespace events collection (collection.typeName events-stacked), confirmed by the working ?format=json door. The org publishes a fresh item for every month of each recurring social — Monthly Trivia, Bear Tea, Alley Bears, the virtual membership meeting, Bears Brews & Boys — so the 22 upcoming rows are 5 series + 5 one-offs, not 22 events. Cadence words live in the item body/excerpt ("Always the 3rd Thursday of the month", "every third Sunday"); where the site says only "monthly" the day-of-month rule is proven from the listed dates and the past[] instances and said so in the event note. Venues are all third-party (The Alley Bar, Club Cafe, Jacques' Cabaret, Dorchester Brewing Company, Red Room in Provincetown) — Mass Bears and Cubs is an organization, not a bar, so defaults carry no bar. The feed's markerLat/markerLng is the Squarespace default marker on 19 of 22 rows and must not be used as coordinates.

coverage.basis: Single feed door read in full: ?format=json returns upcoming[] with 22 rows and no pagination on the upcoming side (Squarespace paginates only past[]). The static /events page renders the same 22 upcoming article blocks. Collapse: Monthly Trivia ×4, Bear Tea ×4, Alley Bears Gear Night ×4, Monthly Membership Meetings ×3 and Bears Brews & Boys ×2 are five recurring socials published one item per month → 5 series (17 rows); the remaining 5 rows are one-offs → 5 singles (The Belly Party Sep 12, MA Bear Contest Meet & Greet Oct 9, MA Bear Contest 2027 Oct 10, The Belly Party Spooky Bear Oct 30 in Provincetown, Bear Boutique Nov 15). publishedEventCount = 5 + 5 = 10. Every series occurrence is a dated item in the feed (origin listed, one jsonPath each); the window runs to 2026-12-31 because the feed lists December instances for three of the five series. Past listings: past[] page 1 holds 30 rows (2026-09-02 back to 2026-05-06) with pagination.nextPage true; collection.itemCount is 83, so the archive is deeper than the 30 shown — counted, not enumerated, and not paged (no further requests were spent).
knownGaps: past[] beyond page 1 (offset pagination) was not pulled; the past count is 30 shown + an unknown remainder (collection.itemCount 83 covers upcoming and past together).
Bears, Brews & Boys lists no September 2026 instance and no December instance; the file records only the two listed dates.
Item bodies were read from the feed's body HTML; the six cached item pages were checked for extra fields (none) but the remaining 16 item pages were not opened.

traps.label: past[] / <div class="eventlist eventlist--past"> — 30 already-happened items from "Sep 2 Monthly Membership Meetings" back to "May 6 Monthly Membership Meetings", with more behind pagination
traps.why: The configured page renders the past section below the upcoming one, and the JSON door returns them as past[] (pageSize 30, nextPage true). They are earlier instances of the same five series plus one-offs (Jocks at Jacques Aug 28, Bears at the Beach Aug 1, Bearzaar Jun 14, Bear Pride Cruise Jun 7, WOOF Block Party Jun 6, Belly Parties). Under the global allowPastEvents: true the 2026-09-12 trial run extracted all 30 alongside the 22 upcoming (52 records) — that is expected behaviour, but they must never be counted against publishedEventCount, which covers upcoming only.

traps.label: Four "Monthly Trivia" items, four "Bear Tea" items, four "Alley Bears - Gear Night" items, three "Monthly Membership Meetings" items, two "Bears, Brews & Boys" items — one per month, identical body and flyer, distinct fullUrl suffixes (…-ptdw8, …-ptdw8-xf7ff, …-xf7ff-t38z3, …)
traps.why: Squarespace has no recurrence, so the org hand-copies each item month by month (the slug grows a new suffix each copy). They are instances of one series, not 17 separate events: a run that emits 17 one-off records is not wrong per se (each is a real dated instance) but a run that emits a different title per instance, or re-dates one, is. The per-instance pages are the only place the month's own flyer lives (Alley Bears 1.jpg/2.jpg/3.jpg/4.jpg).

openQuestions.q: Should the scraper discard Squarespace's default map marker (markerLat 40.7207559 / markerLng -74.0007613, repeated on 19 of 22 rows and in every per-item ICS GEO line) instead of treating it as venue coordinates? The Boston items would otherwise be placed in Manhattan.

The virtual "Monthly Membership Meetings" publish location title "Online/Virtual" with no address; the 2026-09-12 trial run gave those records city "unknown". Whether an online org meeting belongs on a bar calendar at all is a bear-pass / policy call, not a recon one.
